source: Manual domain labelling of the 24 candidate outcome markers, checked against the log itself (see 'evidence_used' below). BPIC2015 is Dutch municipal building-permit handling under the Wabo / omgevingsvergunning regime.
why_manual: The automatic name-based classifier scores an activity name against a rejection anchor phrase.
It recognised only 3 of the 24 BPIC2015 outcome markers as negative, missing obvious ones such as
'phase procedure aborted' and 'decision permanent suspension irrevocable', because the wording is
Dutch administrative English the sentence model has not seen. With almost every ending scored as
positive, a purely random policy reached a 'good' outcome in 96% of episodes and the outcome metric
carried no information. This file replaces that guess with an explicit, reviewable decision.
labelling_principle: good    - the applicant's outcome is settled and positive: the permit exists and can no longer be challenged.
bad     - the applicant's outcome is settled and negative: no permit will follow.
exclude - the activity happens near the end but does not settle anything. Removed from the terminal
set entirely rather than counted as a success.
evidence_used: A label of 'bad' was only kept where the log shows the case does NOT recover. For each candidate we
measured how often a case that reaches it later reaches a settled-positive marker:
objection lodged against decision ....... 79% later reach a positive settlement -> exclude, not an outcome
set phase decision revoked .............. 48% -> exclude (a revoked decision is often re-issued)
An objection or an appeal is a negative *event* during handling, not a negative *outcome*. Treating
them as outcomes was our first attempt and the log contradicted it, so they were reclassified.
'close case', 'phase archived case' and 'phase case handled' are excluded for the opposite reason:
they occur on granted and refused cases alike, so they record that handling stopped, not how it ended.
consequences: 43.1% of real cases reach one. The other 57% never record a settled outcome in this log.
Of the cases that do: 82.7% positive, 17.3% negative — plausible for building permits.
Median 48 steps to the first settled outcome, against a median trace length of 45.
caveat: These are our readings of the activity names plus the recovery evidence above, not the judgement of a municipal case handler. The weakest point is coverage: for 57% of cases this log never records whether the applicant ended up with a permit, so BPIC2015 outcome results describe a minority of cases and must be reported that way.

set phase: phase permitting irrevocable.label: good
set phase: phase permitting irrevocable.why: The permit has become irrevocable — the objection and appeal windows have closed with the permit standing. The definitive positive settlement. Present in 35.6% of cases.

phase decision irrevocable.label: good
phase decision irrevocable.why: The same settlement recorded at the decision level: the decision can no longer be challenged. Present in 19.7% of cases.

phase procedure aborted.label: bad
phase procedure aborted.why: The procedure was terminated without a decision. No case that reaches this later reaches a positive settlement (0 of 335).

decision permanent suspension irrevocabl.label: bad
decision permanent suspension irrevocabl.why: The case was permanently suspended and that suspension is now final. No case recovers (0 of 146).

copy decision permanent suspension to st.label: bad
copy decision permanent suspension to st.why: Communication step on the permanent-suspension path above. No case recovers (0 of 119).

objection lodged against decision.label: exclude
objection lodged against decision.why: A bezwaar was filed. 79% of these cases still reach a positive settlement afterwards, so this is a negative event during handling, not a negative outcome.

appeal logded.label: exclude
appeal logded.why: A beroep was filed. 69% still settle positively afterwards. (Spelling as recorded in the log.)

contested decision affected.label: exclude
contested decision affected.why: The decision was challenged and altered. 65% still settle positively afterwards.

set phase decision revoked.label: exclude
set phase decision revoked.why: The decision was withdrawn, but 48% of these cases go on to a positive settlement — a revoked decision is commonly replaced by a new one. Too ambiguous to score either way.

close case.label: exclude
close case.why: Administrative closure. Occurs on granted and refused cases alike, so it records that handling stopped rather than how it ended. Strongest raw ending in the log (18.1% of traces) and therefore the most tempting wrong answer.

phase archived case.label: exclude
phase archived case.why: The file was archived. Same reasoning as 'close case' — outcome-neutral.

phase case handled.label: exclude
phase case handled.why: Marks that handling finished, without saying how. Outcome-neutral.

enter senddate decision environmental pe.label: exclude
enter senddate decision environmental pe.why: Records that the decision was posted. The objection window opens here rather than closing, so nothing is settled. Present in 78.7% of cases — treating it as success is what made the metric uninformative.

transcript decision environmental permit.label: exclude
transcript decision environmental permit.why: Distribution of the decision to interested parties. Communication, not conclusion.

phase decision sent.label: exclude
phase decision sent.why: Phase marker for the same dispatch step.

enter senddate decision.label: exclude
enter senddate decision.why: Generic variant of the dispatch step.

enter date publication decision environm.label: exclude
enter date publication decision environm.why: Publication date recorded. Publication starts the appeal clock; it does not end the case.

read publication date field.label: exclude
read publication date field.why: System read of the publication date. Administrative housekeeping.

register deadline.label: exclude
register deadline.why: Registers a future deadline, so by definition the case is still running.

date decision for inspection.label: exclude
date decision for inspection.why: Sets the date the decision becomes available for inspection — a step in the publication sequence.

set decision phase inspection of decisio.label: exclude
set decision phase inspection of decisio.why: Phase marker for the same inspection window.

stop all running subcases 2b.label: exclude
stop all running subcases 2b.why: Closes open subcases. Housekeeping that accompanies a conclusion rather than being one, and it occurs on both positive and negative paths.

continue or abort mutation BAG objects.label: exclude
continue or abort mutation BAG objects.why: Updates the BAG address and buildings registry. A downstream registry action, unrelated to the applicant's outcome.
